title: Pilot adapter & runtime roadmap - HydroLine Utilities POC scoping

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Evan Liu (Redwood Solutions Eng); Marta Reyes (HydroLine Head of Data); Omar Patel (Platform Engineer); Sofia Nguyen (Security Lead); Liam Carter (Product Manager)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Priya and Evan are with me on the technical side. how's everybo– hows it going at HydroLine today?
00:08 Marta: hey thanks, yep all good. appreciate you squeezing this in. we've got a lot to cover around the pilot scope.
00:15 Jordan: cool. high level — we're aiming to define success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, and an integration approach. Priya, i'll hand it off to you to walk through the runtime adapter options.
00:26 Priya: thanks. so two main patterns we recommend: SDK-first integration using Redwood's SDK which gives client-side batching, retries, and an openai-compatible endpoint shim; or an adapter proxy that sits in their infra and translates calls to Redwood hosted/dedicated endpoints. advantages: SDK removes a lot of plumbing for app engineers; adapter gives more control for on-prem VPC constraints.
00:45 Omar: quick q — our traffic flows through a proprietary gateway. can we run the adapter inside our VPC so no egress to the public internet for user data?
00:54 Priya: yes, that's the private deployment pattern — Redwood Private with VPC peering or an on-prem package. we'll need network rules and KMS integration for keys. note: the adapter can be deployed as a small k8s service and talks to Redwood control plane over mTLS; in some transcriptions it shows up as "Redwood predicated" but it's mTLS.
01:15 Sofia: about KMS — we use AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys and we have a strict retention policy. we need to confirm no model inputs or outputs are logged beyond what the pilot requires.
01:26 Evan: understood. we support customer-managed KMS; can limit logging and set audit retention. we'll include an audit log profile for the pilot.
01:35 Marta: success criteria — we want to measure latency p95 under 1.2s for single-turn chat at our median prompt length (~160 tokens) and throughput of 40 rps for batching scenarios, accuracy parity within 3% of current OpenAI responses on our eval set, and total cost under $X per million tokens (placeholder).
02:01 Jordan: good explicit targets. to validate accuracy parity we'll run A/B style blind evals. Priya — the bench harness?
02:09 Priya: plan is to use Redwood's benchmark harness (we call it the "runner") that can replay traffic traces with configurable concurrency, variable sequence lengths, and tokenization alignment. we'll need sample traces and the three canonical prompts from HydroLine. we'll instrument to collect latency histograms, token counts, and KV cache hit rates.
02:31 Omar: we can export traces from our gateway, but the format is slightly custom — we'll deliver a CSV with timestamp, request size, and endpoint. is that ok?
02:39 Priya: that's fine. we can map it; ideally JSONL format with prompt + metadata but CSV is workable. note — sometimes autop-generated transcripts show "CSV layout off" — but we're used to mapping fields.
02:56 Liam: on structured output — our product relies on JSON-LD responses and a set of tool calls (internal lookup and billing API). does Redwood support function/tool calling?
03:08 Evan: yes — Redwood supports tool/function calling and structured output. there are two integration points: 1) using the OpenAI-compatible function calling schema via the adapter/endpoint; 2) directly embedding a small tool runner in the adapter to execute calls against internal microservices. for security we recommend the adapter perform auth and token exchange, then call your internal services behind VPC.
03:33 Sofia: security question — will tool execution require additional audit trails? we need an end-to-end trace of tool inputs/outputs for compliance.
03:43 Priya: yes, we can enable per-tool audit logging and redact secrets. logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog or pushed into a secure S3 bucket with encryption.
03:55 Marta: benchmarks — what are realistic expectations for latency difference between hosted and dedicated?
04:02 Evan: hosted API (multi-tenant) is usually a bit higher tail latency; dedicated GPU pools drop P95 by 20–35% depending on model and batching. for your workload with 160-token median, we estimate p95 ~0.8–1.0s on dedicated and ~1.1–1.6s hosted, but we will validate. quantization and kernel selection can impact regen.
04:28 Omar: ok can we do a quick micro-benchmark next week?
04:32 Priya: yes we'll run a baseline on a small subset; we need a dev endpoint and the traffic sample.
04:38 Jordan: timeline suggestion — 6 week pilot: week 0 (prep & agreements), week 1 (env setup + sample ingestion), week 2 (baseline bench hosted), week 3 (adapter deploy + SDK smoke tests), week 4 (dedicated pilot if you want reserved capacity + deeper bench), week 5 (A/B evals and quality checks), week 6 (wrap, recommendations & SOW).
05:03 Marta: that maps to our Q2 needs. our stakeholders expect a go/no-go decision by end of April.
05:11 Jordan: noted. next — cost modeling. Marta had a placeholder. Jordan: you mentioned cost per 1M tokens — we can provide a scaled estimate for both hosted pay-as-you-go and a committed dedicated price.
05:23 Jordan: i'll get those numbers in the pricing deck. sample estimate will include tokenized counts (prompt vs completion), bench-derived throughput, and reserved capacity uplift.
05:35 Liam: about SDK — do we need to change our existing client code a lot? our front end uses an internal SDK to call the gateway, which then calls the LLM backend.
05:45 Priya: minimal changes — Redwood SDK is drop-in compatible with OpenAI API shapes. you can keep your gateway; we'd either put the SDK in the gateway or use the adapter to translate. in our experience putting SDK in the gateway reduces round trips and preserves batching.
06:05 Omar: any pitfalls on tokenization mismatch? we've seen small differences between models causing prompt truncation.
06:12 Evan: good question. we'll align on tokenizer (BPE vs byte-level) and instrument token counts. bench harness will check for truncation and fallback behaviors. we'll capture the tokenization artifacts and include prompts that sit near the 512 and 1024 boundaries.
06:29 Marta: on fidelity testing — we'll need a blind eval runner. can Redwood run blind A/B tests with our internal raters?
06:36 Priya: yes, we can orchestrate blind sets and provide a simple web UI for raters to score. we'll anonymize which model produced which response.
06:46 Sofia: compliance items — we need SOC2 evidence, encryption in transit and at rest, RBAC for console access and SSO integration (SAML).
06:55 Evan: Redwood supports SSO/SAML, RBAC roles, and SOC2 Type II. we'll attach the compliance pack; note sometimes our docs call out "SOC II" with spacing, but it's the same.
07:08 Jordan: next steps recap — (1) Redwood share benchmark harness and sample repo (Priya/Evan) by 2026-03-08; (2) HydroLine to provide traces and 3 canonical prompts by 2026-03-09; (3) security questionnaire exchange (Sofia + Evan) by 2026-03-10; (4) pricing/SOW draft from Jordan by 2026-03-10; (5) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-15. any other asks?
07:39 Marta: nothing else. thanks.
07:42 Jordan: thanks all. we'll follow up with links and the harness.
07:46 End of meeting

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels approximate; occasional misrecognition of product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" for Redwood Dedicated), and some timestamps are approximate.
